LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Description: Your colony ship reached its destination, but lost its stern and computer core in an attack. You alone are awake. Contact Starbound from the trainer outside the airlock, learn what happened, and prepare for life in space.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_AwaitingWake: Preparing the trainer outside the airlock before the captain wakes.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Welcome: You awaken alone in the damaged forward section. Read the opening account, then find the trainer’s comms console.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Briefing: Hear Starbound’s explanation and agree to begin flight training.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Welcome:
Your cryptosleep casket ejects you. It seems your colony ship has reached its destination.

The place looks thoroughly looted. Apart from the caskets, structural beams, reactor, life support and a few tables and chairs, almost nothing remains—including the computer core that housed the ship AI. Worse, the entire stern is missing. Outside the airlock sits a strange metal box that might be a ship.

Wearing your vacuum gear, you investigate. A device resembling a comms console records an earlier call from an organization calling itself Starbound. Perhaps they know something.

You leave your fellow colonists asleep until you understand the situation. After a packaged survival meal whose expiry date reads “Never”, you consider your options. Calling the mysterious organization seems the only sensible one.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Briefing:
Ah, finally awake?

You caused us quite a bit of trouble, so we took the computer core as compensation. We knocked on your casket and asked permission first. You did not object.

All right, joking aside: your AI’s records say you are this group’s captain. Welcome to the rimworld, and congratulations! You reached the right planet, exactly the one you chose. Your original plans are probably ruined, though. A great deal happened during your interstellar journey: insects, mechanoids, aggressive pig people, the Horax cult and the dark archotechs behind it…

Those of you in the bow were the lucky unlucky ones. Mechanoids spotted your ship on approach and blasted it in two. Three poor souls from the stern apparently escaped in pods and fell to the surface. As I said, a terrible destination. Your section drifted toward our station with a pack of mechanoid ships in pursuit. We worked very hard to keep you from becoming space debris, and dealt with your attackers too. Salvaging some equipment you no longer needed seems fair payment, does it not?

Making a living in space is no small task. In consideration of your computer core, we will teach you how to survive here. That trainer is for practice. Once you can fly properly, we will throw in a research ship with our most advanced technology to make up the difference. Generous, right?
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Leave: End space survival guidance and make my own arrangements.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_OpenDesc: Hear the current briefing again and review the next step.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Targets: View the comms console, captain and training targets
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_MissingArrival: The colony ship’s caskets or captain data are missing. Instruction cannot continue.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_WakeFailed: The captain could not leave the casket. Instruction has stopped; check the cryosleep area.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_PreparingFlight: Preparing the training ship and recovery course.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Flight: Stay aboard the trainer and depart the colony ship. Apply fore/aft, lateral and rotational thrust for at least half a second each, then stop and check in. The course lies outside the colony map boundary.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Salvage: Synchronize velocity with the recovery platform and start exterior work to hard dock. Move 75 steel to the small shelf aboard the training ship, return aboard and check the recovery.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_SoftDock: Depart the recovery site and approach the training shipyard. Enable soft docking guides and align the diamonds of your west port with the yard’s west port. Check once connected.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Visit: Enter the shipyard through the docking port, then follow its east docking passage into the prototype ship. Approach its grav engine and accept the ship. Launching is optional.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Flight:
This public trainer belongs to Starbound Frontier. While allied, you may fly it and use its cargo shelf. You cannot build aboard or claim its facilities; dismantling or attacking them costs goodwill, and losing the alliance also removes access. It has two forward thrusters, two reverse thrusters and two stern lateral RCS units, with no grav engine.

Put on your vacuum suit and helmet, then board through the colony ship's east airlock and the connected passage. Select the trainer, use its flight control and confirm departure. W/S move forward and backward, A/D strafe, Q/E turn. Departure retracts the passage, so get your colonist inside first.

Remember why this ship is awkward: we borrowed its bow RCS units. Watch the forward and reverse engines counter the turning moment while you strafe. Give your own general-purpose ship lateral thrusters at both ends.

Practice each type of movement for at least half a second, then release the controls and let flight assistance slow you down, or use the brake. Stop before checking your progress. Merely entering flight control or pressing one key will not pass.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Salvage:
Recover the steel from the platform, listed among the quest targets outside the colony map. Fly clear of the colony before starting work. Approach, select velocity synchronization, then start exterior work when ready. The structures will share a working map.

Extend a passage from your docking port if needed, or build substructure in unclaimed parts of the work area. You cannot rebuild the public training ship. Keep your vacuum gear on and haul 75 steel to the training ship’s designated small shelf, which prioritizes steel.

Return aboard before checking. You keep the recovered steel.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_SoftDock: Bring yourself and the steel aboard and depart. The training shipyard starts stationary and has no thrusters.\n\nThis time the maps stay separate. Enable the soft docking guides, approach the yard’s west port, and align the paired diamonds. Your port faces west, so turn the ship until the ports face each other. Slow down and maintain alignment until the passage is actually connected, then check in.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Visit:
The passage is connected. Stop manual piloting to control your colonist, enter through your docking port, then walk through the yard’s east docking passage to the prototype ship’s grav engine.

The prototype ship in the berth is yours. The engine is a prototype nobody has dared ride. If you feel the same way, leave it unstarted; thrusters handle ordinary movement in space.

Keep the recovered supplies. The public training ship still belongs to Starbound. Confirm beside the engine to complete this flight and docking course.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_AcceptShip: Accept the ship and complete training.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_FlightProgress: Flight practice: fore/aft {0}/30, lateral {1}/30, rotation {2}/30 game ticks. Finish with your colonist aboard and linear and angular speed near zero.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_SalvageProgress: The training shelf holds {0}/75 steel. Hard dock with the designated recovery platform and return your colonist aboard before checking.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_NeedSoftDock: The designated training-ship and shipyard ports are not connected. Maintain diamond alignment until the connection completes.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_NeedVisit: Bring your colonist beside the prototype’s grav engine. The console and engine must still belong to the same player ship.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_FlightAssetLost: A required training facility has been removed. The course cannot continue; existing people, ships and supplies remain.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_FlightSetupFailed: The training course could not be prepared. Space survival guidance has ended. Check the log; do not generate duplicate ships.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_TrainingAccessLost: The public training ship is no longer available to you. Flight instruction has ended. Existing people, facilities and supplies remain.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_BerthUnavailable: The berth docking passage could not be established. Space survival guidance has ended; check the log.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Contact: Wear your vacsuit and helmet. Board the metal box through the airlock, select your captain, right-click its comms console and call Starbound. The rest of the crew remains in cryptosleep.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Inquiry: The call is connected. Ask Starbound what they want and what happened to your ship.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Contact:
Wear your vacsuit and helmet, then board the metal box through the east airlock and docking passage.

Select your captain, right-click its comms console and call Starbound. The captain must actually reach the powered console and connect the call; opening quest instructions does not make the call.

The other candidates remain in the colony ship’s cryptosleep caskets. Let them sleep for now.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Inquiry: The console answers: “Starbound here. Oh, someone on the colony ship is finally awake?”
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_AskPurpose: Who are you? Why take our computer core and leave this ship here?
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_CommsLost: The trainer’s comms console was lost before first contact. Instruction has ended.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Design: Listen to the maintenance and thruster-layout briefing, then begin flight practice. No repairs or construction are required.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_StartPractice: Understood. Let me try flying it.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Design:
Before flying, a little maintenance theory. Check the hull and airlocks, life support and power, then look for broken thrusters or obstructions behind their nozzles. This lesson is theory only: you do not need to repair anything or build a ship.

Now, this trainer is rather awkward to fly. That is not your fault. It still has two large forward thrusters and two large reverse thrusters, but its only lateral RCS units are the two at the stern, one on each side. We took the two bow units off to test a new ship recently. Nobody has put them back yet.

Unless you have a specific reason not to, put lateral thrusters at both the bow and stern. Otherwise you get this: a small stern thruster acts far from the center of mass, producing a long-lever-arm turning moment. To move sideways without turning, the large forward and reverse thrusters must also fire through their shorter lever arms to counter it. Watch them during your sideways maneuver. All that extra work comes from the layout.

There are sensible exceptions. Your colony ship originally had no reverse thrusters: it had plenty of time to rotate 180 degrees and brake with its main engines. Some warships with a turtle shell of armor on the bow also have almost no forward RCS. They have little need to strafe; they mostly need to turn their toughest face toward the enemy.

So do not copy this trainer as a general-purpose design. Decide how your ship needs to move before sacrificing thrust directions or lever arms.
